svg.title: 2. Backup and restore with AWS Backup
svg.text: Backup account (separate admins, no prod access)
What backup and restore does not give you
Backup and restore on AWS: one backup policy, three copies, and a clean account to restore into
backup policy on the Prod OU
Tag backup:tier=1 on a resource and the policy picks it up.
Nobody has to remember to add new databases to a plan.
VPC, IAM, ASG, ALB as code
Restore into a fresh account when
you cannot trust the original one.
2:10 app tier healthy, smoke tests pass
1. An RTO in minutes: restoring a large database is bound by data size, not by how fast you click.
2. Capacity guarantees: the recovery Region has to have the instance types and the service quotas you need on the day.
3. Confidence, unless you restore on a schedule. A backup you have never restored is a hope, not a recovery point.
4. Protection from your own mistakes if the copies sit in the same account, under the same admins, with the same KMS key.
